# Urgent Heater Repair in a London Tenancy

Your landlord has had written notice since **2026-01-12**, you followed up on **2026-01-20**, and an indoor temperature of **around 14°C in the evenings** is cold enough to justify prompt escalation. In London, the key is to document the defect, keep communication polite and specific, and create a clear paper trail.

## Practical Repair Checklist and Evidence to Keep

| Step | What to do | What to collect | Why it helps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Re-send a short written request today | Copy of email/text/letter | Shows the issue is still live and urgent |
| 2 | State the effect on daily living | Notes on cold rooms, sleep disruption, inability to use rooms normally | Helps show seriousness, not just inconvenience |
| 3 | Log temperatures morning/evening for several days | Date, time, room, temperature, photo of thermometer | Supports the claim that the flat is unreasonably cold |
| 4 | Photograph the heater and any error codes/leaks | Clear photos with date/time if possible | Proves the defect is real and unchanged |
| 5 | Keep a repair timeline | Dates of first report, follow-up, replies, missed appointments | Useful if you escalate to council or court |
| 6 | Save all messages in one folder | Emails, screenshots, letters, call notes | Makes it easy to share with council or adviser |
| 7 | Check your tenancy paperwork | Repair clause, landlord contact details, agent details | Confirms who is responsible and how notice should be served |
| 8 | Escalate if no prompt action | Council environmental health / housing team | Can trigger inspection or enforcement |
| 9 | Consider formal notice if needed | Copy of a formal letter before further action | Strengthens your position if you later seek remedy |

## What to Record as Evidence

- **Temperature log:** room name, time, reading, and how it felt in the flat.
- **Photos/videos:** broken thermostat, boiler/heater display, cold-room setup, any visible fault.
- **Communication trail:** first report, follow-up, any replies, promises, missed visits.
- **Impact notes:** sleeping in coats, using extra heaters, one bedroom becoming unusable, condensation, damp risk.
- **Receipts:** if you had to buy temporary heaters, blankets, or extra electricity, keep receipts.
- **Witness notes:** if a flatmate or visitor can confirm the cold, note their name and date.

## Polite Message Template for Urgent Repair

Subject: Urgent repair request — broken heater in [flat address]

Dear [Landlord/Agent Name],

I am writing to follow up on my previous reports of the broken heater at [flat address]. I first reported this in writing on **12 January 2026** and followed up on **20 January 2026**, but the issue has not yet been repaired.

The flat has been reaching around **14°C in the evenings**, which is uncomfortably cold and affecting normal use of the property. As this is a 2-bedroom flat, the lack of heating is causing a significant problem, especially in the evenings and overnight.

Please arrange an urgent repair and confirm:
- when an engineer will attend,
- whether any parts are required, and
- the expected completion date.

I would appreciate a reply within **48 hours** given the current temperatures. I have kept a log of the issue and can share photos and temperature readings if helpful.

Kind regards,
[Your full name]
[Address]
[Phone number]

## When to Escalate Next

- If you get no meaningful response within a short time, contact your **local council housing/environmental health team** and report a category of **cold housing / heating failure**.
- If the landlord tries to delay without a date, ask for a **specific appointment** in writing.
- If the flat becomes unsafe or uninhabitable, seek advice before arranging repairs yourself or withholding rent.

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Council housing] https://www.gov.uk/find-local-council
Action: [Button: Tenant advice] https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/housing/renting-privately/repairs-in-private-renting/
Action: [Button: Repair rights] https://www.gov.uk/private-renting/repairs

## Sources

- UK landlord repair responsibilities: https://www.gov.uk/private-renting/repairs
- Local council finder: https://www.gov.uk/find-local-council
- Citizens Advice on private renting repairs: https://www.citizensadvice.org.uk/housing/renting-privately/repairs-in-private-renting/
